crime: A girl who had never seen snow until she came to the prison filmed every snowfall at the lake on her phone. Once, she filmed {WITCH_NAME} vanish from her spot on the shore and reappear there an hour of snowfall later, then asked her how deep it had gotten. She was the only one {WITCH_NAME} told the depths to.
At the first flakes of the next snowfall, the girl said as she set up her phone, "I don't need to know how deep it gets. I just like hearing you talk."

Years before, {WITCH_NAME} had read the depths from her snow notebook at dinner, and her father had answered, "Nobody needs to know how deep the snow is." The table laughed. She never measured snow again, not until the lake.
While the first flakes fell, she twisted the phone strap around the girl's neck until the girl was still.

When the shore had turned white, she pulled on the girl's red mitten and started the recording, so that it opened on the red mitten over a shore already white. Then she put the mitten back on the dead girl's hand, walked to her spot, and vanished on camera.

The prisoners found the girl strangled beside her phone, still recording. On the screen, snow fell on an empty spot where {WITCH_NAME} had stood. At the end of the hour, {WITCH_NAME} reappeared on that spot before them, standing on an hour of untouched snow.
In the trial court, the prisoners concluded that the girl had started the recording herself, and that another hand had strangled her while {WITCH_NAME} was gone.

But the prisoner who had lifted her body from the shore said the grass beneath it was bare and green. The court understood: the girl had lain there before the snow did, so the red mitten at the lens had been on {WITCH_NAME}'s hand.
fields.epitaph: In the end, a whole court needed to know how deep the snow was.
fields.epithet: The Snow-Measurer Nobody Wanted to Hear
execution: The execution stand raised a giant iron clock face. She was chained upright against the twelve.
The iron minute hand ticked toward twelve, one loud tick at a time, in a silent court.
She shut her eyes and opened them. The hand had moved only one tick.
Tick by tick, it brought its edge into her side.
At twelve, the hand stopped across her. She hung still, and the ticking ended.

magic.name: The Skipped Hour
magic.text: She vanishes and reappears on the same spot later, skipping straight past the time between.
